questions.question: When does F_p contain a primitive n-th root of unity?
options: When n divides p-1
When p divides n
When n is prime
When p equals n plus one
questions.explanation: The multiplicative group F_p* has order p-1. A subgroup of order n exists exactly when n divides p-1.

questions.question: What is a primitive n-th root of unity?
options: An element with multiplicative order exactly n
Any element whose n-th power is zero
The smallest element satisfying x^n = 1
An element equal to the field generator raised to n
questions.explanation: Primitive means generating the full cyclic subgroup of order n. The order must be exactly n, not any proper divisor of n.

questions.question: How do you find a primitive n-th root of unity in F_p when n divides p-1?
options: Raise a primitive root g to the power (p-1)/n
Take any element and reduce it modulo n
Compute n modulo p and test each result
Multiply the n-th prime by the field characteristic
questions.explanation: g^((p-1)/n) has order exactly n because g has order p-1 and (p-1)/n is the minimal reduction that keeps the result nontrivial.

questions.question: What identity connects all cyclotomic polynomials?
options: x^n - 1 equals the product of Phi_d for all divisors d of n
Phi_n equals x^n minus the sum of all smaller cyclotomic polynomials
x^n + 1 factors as the product of Phi_d for prime d only
Phi_n evaluated at 1 always equals the characteristic of the field
questions.explanation: Every divisor d of n contributes one cyclotomic factor Phi_d. Their product recovers x^n - 1, and this drives the recursive construction.

questions.question: What is the degree of the n-th cyclotomic polynomial?
options: Euler's totient phi(n)
n minus one
The largest prime factor of n
The number of divisors of n
questions.explanation: Phi_n has exactly phi(n) roots — the primitive n-th roots — so its degree equals phi(n).

questions.question: Why does an NTT of length n require n to divide p-1?
options: The transform needs a primitive n-th root of unity as a twiddle factor
Dividing by n requires n to be the field characteristic
The polynomial x^n - 1 must be irreducible over F_p
The NTT butterfly network only works for prime-length inputs
questions.explanation: Each butterfly stage multiplies by successive powers of a primitive n-th root omega. That root only exists in F_p when n divides p-1.

questions.question: What goes wrong if you run an NTT with a prime p where n does not divide p-1?
options: You get fewer than n distinct roots, making the twiddle factors repeat and the transform matrix singular
The field characteristic changes and addition wraps incorrectly
The primitive root raises to a complex number instead of a field element
Every output becomes zero because the polynomial has no roots
questions.explanation: Without n | (p-1) there are only gcd(n, p-1) roots of unity instead of n, so twiddle factors repeat and the DFT matrix is rank-deficient.

questions.question: How does the multiplicative order algorithm avoid testing all values from 1 to p-1?
options: It starts from p-1 and divides down by prime factors as long as a^(order/q) equals 1
It uses the extended Euclidean algorithm on a and p
It factors the polynomial x^a - 1 over F_p directly
It squares a repeatedly until the result exceeds p
questions.explanation: The order divides p-1 by Lagrange's theorem. Dividing by each prime factor q while the power test still returns 1 finds the minimum order efficiently.
